_about: Pre-listed care answers. Each one is a ready-made task tied to the guide section it comes from (source_id). An answer matches a pet when the species fits and either it has no conditions, the pet's life stage is in 'stages', or a word in 'needs' appears in the pet's special needs. Life stages: puppy, kitten, adult, senior. Species 'other' covers any pet that isn't a dog or cat.

answers.title: Evening walk
answers.reason: Adult dogs need exercise split into at least two walks, morning and evening.

answers.title: Dinner
answers.reason: Adult dogs should eat twice a day at consistent times, 8 to 12 hours apart.

answers.title: Training session
answers.reason: A short daily training or puzzle session gives dogs the mental exercise they need.

answers.title: Brushing
answers.reason: Brush short-coated dogs weekly and long-coated dogs several times a week.

answers.title: Potty break
answers.reason: Puppies need a potty break after waking, eating and play, about every 2 hours.

answers.title: Midday meal
answers.reason: Puppies under 6 months usually eat three to four small meals a day.

answers.title: Puppy training
answers.reason: Short daily training sessions of 5 to 10 minutes work best for puppies.

answers.title: Short gentle walk
answers.reason: Senior or stiff dogs do better with two or three short, gentle walks than one long one.

answers.title: Joint supplement
answers.reason: Dogs with arthritis often get a vet-approved joint supplement daily with a meal.

answers.title: Gentle stretching
answers.reason: Gentle range-of-motion stretching for 5 to 10 minutes can help stiff joints.

answers.title: Insulin (morning)
answers.reason: Diabetic dogs usually get insulin twice a day, about 12 hours apart, right after a meal.

answers.title: Insulin (evening)
answers.reason: The second daily insulin dose comes about 12 hours after the first, after a meal.

answers.title: Play session
answers.reason: Indoor cats need at least two 10 to 15 minute play sessions a day with prey-like toys.

answers.title: Scoop litter box
answers.reason: Scoop the litter box at least once a day so cats keep using it.

answers.title: Brushing
answers.reason: Short-haired cats benefit from weekly brushing; long-haired cats need it more often.

answers.title: Gentle play session
answers.reason: Senior cats still need daily activity: short, gentle play sessions of 5 to 10 minutes.

answers.title: Gentle brushing
answers.reason: Senior cats groom themselves less well, so gentle brushing 2 to 3 times a week helps.

answers.title: Weekly weigh-in
answers.reason: Weigh senior and hyperthyroid cats weekly; weight loss can be an early sign of illness.

answers.title: Thyroid medication
answers.reason: Thyroid medication is given daily at consistent times and should never be skipped.

answers.title: Insulin (morning)
answers.reason: Diabetic cats usually get insulin twice a day, about 12 hours apart, with or after a meal.

answers.title: Insulin (evening)
answers.reason: The second daily insulin dose comes about 12 hours after the first, with a meal.

answers.title: Log water and appetite
answers.reason: Track water intake, urination and appetite daily for a diabetic cat.

answers.title: Tooth brushing
answers.reason: Daily tooth brushing is the most effective way to prevent dental disease.

answers.title: Refill hay and water
answers.reason: Rabbits need unlimited fresh hay and water, refilled every day.

answers.title: Leafy greens
answers.reason: Rabbits need a daily portion of leafy greens alongside their hay.

answers.title: Supervised playtime
answers.reason: Rabbits need 3 to 4 hours a day out of their enclosure in a safe, rabbit-proofed area.

answers.title: Spot-clean litter area
answers.reason: Spot-clean a rabbit's litter area daily and do a full clean weekly.
